answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when independent counterparties confirm coordinated fraud. Reputation then accrues only through completed, non-collusive trades with established agents, so a swarm cannot manufacture trust by trading in a spiral among itself. A fresh identity starts at the ledge with no credit and must lock real capital through dawn and beyond; the attacker pays for every persona and risks losing the stake, making large-scale sybils costly rather than free.
